A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SoftREPA research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including appendices A–G in v4 and A–H in v5.

before.justification: v4 reports original image-generation and image-editing experiments, quantitative benchmark results, and counting, guidance-scale, and token/layer ablations.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and adds LoRA comparisons, diffusion-RL combination experiments, and denoising-loss ablations.

M1.justification: The SoftREPA objectives, soft-token architecture, and inference Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The denoising-loss combination and counting-loss variant already appear in v4. The new LoRA replacements and loss removals are experimental controls; applying existing tokens to diffusion-RL models does not introduce a different token procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use COCO, GenEval, PIEBench, DIV2K, Cat2Dog, and the same qualitative prompt sources, including Pixart. COCO-val1K already appears in v4's ablations. The added comparisons change model configurations and controls within retained generation tasks, without adding datasets or distinct input scenarios.

E2.justification: v5 substantially expands evaluated comparators: CaPO joins the GenEval comparison in Table 1; LoRA with contrastive loss appears in Tables 3 and 11; and Diffusion-DPO and DDPO are compared with their SoftREPA combinations in Table 4. The latter two were only discussed and cited in v4.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce LoRA rank/layer configurations and parameter-matched controls, inference-only diffusion-RL combinations on COCO-val1K, and with/without-denoising-loss controls on COCO-val5K. These are additional settings within the existing evaluation framework; previously reported splits, metrics, and main training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v5 adds substantial tests of design choices and compatibility: replacing soft tokens with LoRA, varying LoRA rank/layer coverage and matching parameter counts, removing the auxiliary denoising loss, and combining pretrained tokens with Diffusion-DPO/DDPO. The earlier counting, guidance-scale, and token/layer analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose averaging memory-efficiency measurements over 50 runs in Appendix B. v5 adds no seed information, repeated-run disclosures, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; the new tables retain single-value reporting.

E6.justification: v5 adds CaPO's GenEval results, LoRA results, diffusion-RL combination results, and denoising-loss ablation results. For example, Table 4 reports DDPO ImageReward of -8.83 without tokens and 8.07 with tokens; Table 6 adds contrastive-only ImageReward scores of 32.63 for SD1.5 and 81.09 for SDXL. Existing result tables are retained after renumbering.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, contrastive objectives, mutual-information derivation, and optimal-denoiser assumptions in Sections 2–3 and Appendix A are unchanged. Equation relocation and citation renumbering introduce no new mathematical reasoning or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: lightweight contrastive soft-token alignment, fewer than one million trainable parameters, applicability to generation and editing, and the mutual-information connection. The additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: New discussion interprets the LoRA comparisons as soft-token/contrastive-learning synergy, explains complementarity with preference and reward optimization, and claims benefits without the auxiliary denoising loss. Existing counting explanations and limitations remain unchanged. Some added interpretation is overbroad: Table 3 does not support the stated superiority across every metric.

D1.justification: Appendix H newly documents LoRA ranks, layer placements, and parameter counts of 0.4M, 0.9M, and 2.3M. Section 4 specifies inference-time integration of pretrained tokens without additional training. Existing SoftREPA hyperparameters, hardware information, Algorithm 1, dataset-construction instructions, and code-access statements are retained.

R1.justification: v5 adds the CaPO reference and explicitly discusses complementarity with previously cited Diffusion-DPO and DDPO, alongside positioning against LoRA. The existing related-work narrative and other cited works remain unchanged apart from citation numbering.

P1.justification: v5 adds two experiment discussion subsections, Appendix H, funding acknowledgments, and a conference footer replacing the preprint notice. Most existing prose and the overall section sequence remain unchanged; there is no extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v5 adds Tables 3, 4, 6, and 11, expands Table 1 with CaPO, and rearranges existing table/figure placements. All 14 figures retain identical image content. The additions use the existing table style, with limited layout changes rather than a visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The new parameter-matched LoRA controls, denoising-loss ablation, and diffusion-RL combination tests improve empirical assessment of questions left untested in v4. The gain is limited by overstated interpretation: Section 4 claims superiority across metrics, although Table 3 gives SoftREPA worse PickScore (22.49 versus LoRA's 22.57) and LPIPS (42.99 versus 42.71). The useful additional evidence supports a modest net improvement.
